summary: Feed s111_double to SIEM is degraded: 9.0% duplicate packets waste capacity and 4.62 Gbps microbursts overload the 1 Gbps SIEM port causing drops and detection gaps.

findings.root_cause: Same packets arriving via multiple SPAN/TAP ingress ports aggregated to one SIEM output without deduplication at the packet broker - 301 of 3331 packets (9.0%) are duplicates exceeding 5% threshold.
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM wastes EPS/license/storage processing duplicates, inflates event counts and correlation, and reduces effective detection coverage.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication to drop duplicate copies before SIEM, restoring accurate counts and freeing bandwidth for unique events.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker forwards unshaped microbursts peaking at 4.62 Gbps in 1ms intervals to a 1 Gbps SIEM port (462% of capacity, 3 overloaded intervals).
findings.impact_on_tool: SIEM ingress port drops packets during bursts, creating blind spots and missed security events; SIEM cannot keep up with peak rate.

recommended_fix.why: Distribute traffic across multiple SIEM receivers or add filtering/slicing (SIEM needs_full_payload=false) to keep per-port rate below 1 Gbps and prevent burst drops.
